
# Supplementary Figure 5 - growth curve analysis

# +++ Setup

## Libraries

Load necessary libraries for data analysis and plotting.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(conflicted)
library(gcplyr)
library(egg)

library(ggpubr)
library(colorspace)

library(readxl)

conflict_prefer("select", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("combine", "dplyr")
```

## Metadata

```{r}
# Load metadata

tab2_PlateLayout = readxl::read_excel(file.path(dir_input, "Tab2_PlateLayout.xlsx"))
```

## List of Runs

```{r}
# -----------------------------
# Function: sort file names based on RUN number (case-insensitive)
# -----------------------------

## ******************************************************************************
# Sort runs
func_sort_by_run = function(file_list) {
  # Extract the RUN number from each element of the vector
  run_nums = gsub(".*RUN([0-9]+).*", "\\1", file_list, ignore.case = TRUE)
  # Convert run numbers to numeric values
  run_nums = as.numeric(run_nums)
  # Sort vector based on numbers
  sorted_list = file_list[order(run_nums)]
  # Return the sorted vector
  return(sorted_list)
}
## ******************************************************************************
```

```{r}
## ______________________________________________________
# List raw data files
list_of_files = list.files(dir_input, pattern = "RUN")

# Sort list of files
list_of_files = func_sort_by_run(file_list = list_of_files)
```

## Load raw data

```{r}
# -----------------------------
# Function: load and combine raw data for all runs based on metadata
# -----------------------------

## ******************************************************************************
func_read_data = function(file_list, run_layout, plate_layout, start_row) {
  
  # Extract all run number from the file list
  all_file_run_numbers = as.numeric(gsub(".*RUN([0-9]+).*", "\\1", file_list, ignore.case = TRUE))
  all_metadata_run_numbers = run_layout$RUN
  
  # Create error message if there are run numbers in the file list that are not in the metadata
  if (!all(all_file_run_numbers %in% all_metadata_run_numbers)) {
    stop("***Mighty error: There are run numbers in the file list that are not in the metadata.***")
  }
  
  # Map run numbers to file names to easily access the correct file for each run number
  run_file_map = setNames(file_list, all_file_run_numbers)
  
  # initialize list to store data for all runs
  all_runs_data_list = list()
  
  ## ______________________________________________________
  # Loop through files
  for (run_num in all_file_run_numbers) {
    
    # Create error message if there are run numbers in the metadata that are not in the file list
    if (is.na(run_file_map[as.character(run_num)])) {
      stop(paste("No file found for RUN", run_num))
    }
    
    # Extract number of plates for this run from metadata
    all_num_plates = run_layout %>% dplyr::filter(RUN == run_num) %>% dplyr::pull(RUN.plate)
    
    # initialize list to store data for this run
    run_data_list = list()
    
    ## ______________________________________________________
    # Loop through plates
    for (plate_num in all_num_plates) {
      
      # print message to track progress
      message(paste0("Reading data for RUN ", run_num, " - PLATE ", plate_num))
      
      # extract time metadata for this plate from metadata
      TIME.duration = run_layout %>% dplyr::filter(RUN == run_num, RUN.plate == plate_num) %>% dplyr::pull(TIME.duration)
      TIME.interval = run_layout %>% dplyr::filter(RUN == run_num, RUN.plate == plate_num) %>% dplyr::pull(TIME.interval)
      
      # define end row based on time metadata
      end_row = start_row + TIME.duration
      
      # Read data for this plate
      data = readxl::read_excel(file.path(dir_input, run_file_map[as.character(run_num)]), 
        sheet = plate_num,
        skip = start_row -1,
        n_max = end_row - start_row + 1,
        col_names = TRUE
      )
      
      # Adjust data
      data = data %>% 
        dplyr::select(-"T° 578") %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(Time = 0:TIME.duration*TIME.interval) %>% 
        tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -Time, names_to = "WELL", values_to = "OD") %>%
        dplyr::mutate(OD = as.numeric(OD),
                      rrpp = run_num*100 + plate_num) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(TIME = Time)
      
      # Add metadata to data
      metadata_RunLayout = run_layout %>% 
        filter(RUN == run_num, RUN.plate == plate_num) %>% 
        select(-TIME.duration, -TIME.interval)
      
      data = data %>% 
        dplyr::bind_cols(metadata_RunLayout[rep(1, nrow(data)), ])
      
      # Store data for this plate in the list for this run
      run_data_list[[plate_num]] = data
    }
  
    # Combine data for all plates in this run into a single data frame
    run_data = dplyr::bind_rows(run_data_list)
  
    # Store data for this run in the list for all runs
    all_runs_data_list[[run_num]] = run_data
  }
  
  # Combine data for all runs into a single data frame
  all_runs_data = dplyr::bind_rows(all_runs_data_list)

  # Add metadata from plate layout to the combined data for all runs
  all_runs_data = all_runs_data %>% 
    dplyr::left_join(plate_layout, by = c("PLATE.design", "WELL"))
  
  # Factor wells to be in correct order
  all_runs_data = all_runs_data %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(WELL = factor(WELL, levels = paste0(rep(LETTERS[1:8], each = 12), 1:12, sep = "")))
  
  # Return combined data for all runs
  return(all_runs_data)
}
## ******************************************************************************
```

```{r}
## ______________________________________________________
# Load data for all runs
df_master = func_read_data(file_list = list_of_files, 
                           run_layout = tab1_RunLayout,
                           plate_layout = tab2_PlateLayout,
                           start_row = 40
                           )
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------

# +++ Baseline correction - LM

To account for compound-specific optical background effects, baseline correction is performed per well. For each curve a log-linear model is fitted to the early time points and extrapolated to t = 0 to estimate the initial optical density. This estimated baseline is then subtracted from all time points of the corresponding well, allowing correction for well-specific baseline shifts without assuming exponential growth.

## Estimate baseline per well

### Medium control slope Correction

To control for systematic medium-driven temporal effects, such as optical relaxation, temperature equilibration, or compound absorbance decay, the slope of all medium control curves per-plate is calculated and subtracted from all curves on a per-well basis.

```{r}
## ______________________________________________________
# Calculate medium control median
baseline_medium = df_master %>%
  dplyr::filter(CONDITION == "Control_Medium") %>% 
  dplyr::select(rrpp, WELL, TIME, OD)

## ______________________________________________________
# Calculate slope of medium control curves per plate
baseline_medium_fit = baseline_medium %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(rrpp) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    blank_intercept = coef(lm(OD ~ TIME))[1],
    blank_slope = coef(lm(OD ~ TIME))[2],
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## ____________________________________________________
# Subtract medium control from all data points to account for medium-specific background effects
df_corr = df_master %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(baseline_medium_fit, by = c("rrpp")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    OD.corr.med = OD - blank_slope * TIME
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-blank_intercept, -blank_slope)

```

### Calculate and subtract baseline

After adjusting for medium-specific temporal effects, the baseline is estimated for each curve by fitting a log-linear model to the early time points and extrapolating to t = 0. This estimated baseline is then subtracted from all time points of the corresponding curve to get the t0-corrected curves.

```{r}
## ______________________________________________________
# Alternative baseline estimation using log-transformed linear fit to early time points
baseline_estimates = df_corr %>%
  dplyr::group_by(rrpp, WELL) %>%
  # Use early time window
  dplyr::filter(TIME <= 4) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(
    intercept = stats::coef(lm(log(OD.corr.med) ~ TIME))[1],
    ODt0      = exp(intercept),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(rrpp, WELL, ODt0)

## ______________________________________________________
# Add baseline estimates to growth curve data and perform baseline correction
df_corr = df_corr %>%
  dplyr::left_join(baseline_estimates, by = c("rrpp", "WELL")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(OD.corr.t0 = OD.corr.med - ODt0)
```

### Set floor for negative values

To avoid issues with negative values after baseline correction, which can cause problems for log-transformation and derivative calculations, we can set a floor value for all t0-corrected OD values. This ensures that all values are positive and allows for downstream analyses without errors. Negative OD values close to 0 are not biologically meaningful and represent baseline correction noise.

```{r}
## ______________________________________________________
# Set floor for negative values after baseline correction
df_corr = df_corr %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(OD.corr.t0 = ifelse(OD.corr.t0 < 0.001, 0.001, OD.corr.t0))
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------

# +++ Curve noise reduction

## calculate smoothed curves

```{r}
## ______________________________________________________
# Apply two-step smoothing for noise reduction
df_smooth = df_corr %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(rrpp, WELL) %>%
  mutate(
    OD.smoothed_medi = gcplyr::smooth_data(x = TIME, y = OD.corr.t0, sm_method = "moving-median", window_width_n = 3),
    OD.smoothed_medi = ifelse(is.na(OD.smoothed_medi), OD.corr.t0, OD.smoothed_medi),
    OD.smoothed_mean = gcplyr::smooth_data(x = TIME, y = OD.smoothed_medi, sm_method = "moving-average", window_width_n = 3),
    OD.smoothed_mean = ifelse(is.na(OD.smoothed_mean), OD.smoothed_medi, OD.smoothed_mean)
    ) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------

# +++ Calculate growth metrics

## Calculate derivatives

Lag time calculation require the calculation of derivatives.

```{r}
## _____________________________________________________
# calculate simdple and per-capita derivative for smoothed curves
df_deriv = df_smooth %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(rrpp, WELL) %>%
  mutate(deriv.simple = gcplyr::calc_deriv(x = TIME, y = OD.smoothed_mean, window_width_n = 3)) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

## Metrics

Note: NAs will mostly always be calculated, as the calculations are done per well and controls are filtered out in later steps.

```{r}
## ______________________________________________________
# Calculate growth metrics
df_metrics = df_deriv %>%
  dplyr::group_by(rrpp, WELL, CONDITION, SPECIES.name, DRUG.name, CONCENTRATION, REPLICATE) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    
    # timepoint of max growth rate:
    time.infliction = gcplyr::extr_val(TIME, which_max_gc(deriv.simple)),
    
    # lag time:
    time.lag = gcplyr::lag_time(x = TIME, y = OD.corr.t0, deriv = deriv.simple, trans_y = "linear"),
    
    # time of end of exponential phase:
    time.end.expo = time.infliction + (time.infliction-time.lag),
    
    # growth curve area under the curve:
    AUC = gcplyr::auc(x = TIME, y = OD.smoothed_medi),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### Calculate gc-end-exponential AUCs

To analyse the AUC of treated wells against the AUC of growth controls, but at the end of the exponential phase of the growth controls, we need to calculate the time of the end of the exponential phase for each growth control curve. This can be done by calculating the lag time and infliction point for each growth control curve and then using these to calculate the end of the exponential phase. Once we have the time of the end of the exponential phase for each growth control curve, we can calculate the AUC up to that time point for all curves.

```{r}
## ______________________________________________________
# Calculate metrics of growth controls per species
df_metrics_controls_temp = df_deriv %>%
  dplyr::group_by(rrpp, WELL, CONDITION, SPECIES.name) %>%
  dplyr::filter(CONDITION == "Control_Growth") %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(
    time.infliction.gc = gcplyr::extr_val(TIME, which_max_gc(deriv.simple)),
    time.lag.gc = gcplyr::lag_time(x = TIME, y = OD.corr.t0, deriv = deriv.simple, trans_y = "linear"),
    time.end.expo.gc = time.lag.gc + (time.infliction.gc - time.lag.gc),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(rrpp, CONDITION, SPECIES.name) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    time.end.expo.gc.median = median(time.end.expo.gc, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## ______________________________________________________
# Join control metrics with main metrics data frame
df_metrics_controls = df_deriv %>%
  dplyr::left_join(df_metrics_controls_temp, by = c("rrpp", "SPECIES.name")) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(rrpp, WELL) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
     AUC.expo.end.gc = {
      # Get unique time.end.expo.gc.median value for the current group because its not collapsed yet
      t_end = unique(time.end.expo.gc.median)
      # Check if t_end is a single value, not NA, and greater than 0 before calculating AUC
      if (length(t_end) == 1 &&
          !is.na(t_end) &&
          t_end > 0) {
        # Calculate AUC up to the end of exponential phase of the growth control for the corresponding species and plate
        gcplyr::auc(x = TIME,y = OD.smoothed_medi,xlim = c(0, t_end))
        } else {NA}
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## ______________________________________________________
# Join gc-end-expo AUCs with main metrics data frame
df_metrics = df_metrics %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(df_metrics_controls, by = c("rrpp", "WELL"))
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------

# +++ Filter Data

Filter out wells with abnormal growth due to technical issues or contamination.

Removed data:
 
-  Replicate 2 of C. comes due to errors in media production. Errors in media creation (missing components) lead to severly increased lagtime of C. comes in replicate 2. This can result in skewed data that does not accurately reflect the true growth characteristics of the species under study. By removing this replicate, we ensure that our analysis is based on reliable controls and representative data.

## Filter data

```{r}
## ______________________________________________________
# Add well run-run-plate-plate-well-well identifyer
df_processed = df_metrics %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(rrpp) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(rrppww = rrpp * 100 + row_number()) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup()


## ______________________________________________________
# Filter data 
df_processed = df_processed %>% 
  dplyr::filter(CONDITION != "Control_Medium",  # Remove medium controls for clarity in downstream analysis and visualization
                !(rrpp == 202 & SPECIES.name == "C.comes") # C.comes replicate 2 removed due to errors in media production
                )
```

## growth curves

### Panel A - Chenodeoxycholic acid

```{r}
## _____________________________________________________
# Growth curve C. comes

# prepare data
plot_data = df_corr %>% 
  filter(SPECIES.name == "C.comes",
         DRUG.name %in% c("DMSO", "BA-4"),
         REPLICATE %in% c(1, 3)) %>% 
  mutate(DRUG.name = recode(DRUG.name,
                         "BA-4" = "Chenodeoxycholic acid",
                         "DMSO" = "DMSO"
                         )) %>% 
  mutate(DRUG.name = factor(DRUG.name, levels = c("DMSO","Chenodeoxycholic acid")))

# Save data:
data_A_comes = plot_data %>% 
                      select(SPECIES.name, DRUG.name, REPLICATE, TIME, OD.corr.t0) %>% 
                      group_by(SPECIES.name, DRUG.name, REPLICATE, TIME) %>% 
                      summarise(OD.corr.t0 = mean(OD.corr.t0), .groups = "drop")
# writexl::write_xlsx(data_A_comes, file.path(dir_output, "Manuscript_figures_data", "A_growth_curves_Ccomes_chenodeoxycholic_acid.xlsx"))

# plot
ggplot(data = plot_data, aes(x = TIME, y = OD.corr.t0, color = DRUG.name, fill = DRUG.name, shape = DRUG.name)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 0.25, show.legend = FALSE) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 1, color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(stat = "summary", fun.data = mean_sd, linewidth = 0.25, width = 0.22, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DMSO" = "grey25", "Chenodeoxycholic acid" = "#006290")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("DMSO" = "grey25", "Chenodeoxycholic acid" = "#006290")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("DMSO" = 5, "Chenodeoxycholic acid" = 21)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.1))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  # geom_vline(xintercept = 7, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 9, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  # annotate("text", x = 7.5, y = 1, label = "t-microscopy", size = 4/.pt, hjust = 1.15, vjust = 0, color = "grey10") +
  annotate("text", x = 9.5, y = 0, label = "AUC.expo.end.gc", size = 4/.pt, hjust = 0, vjust = 0, color = "grey10") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 6) +
  labs(
    title = "C. comes (n = 2)",
    y = "OD578 (t0-corrected)",
    x = "Time (h)",
    ) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.margin = margin(grid::unit(0, "cm")),
    legend.key.height = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"),
    )

# egg
plot_egg = egg::set_panel_size(last_plot(), 
                               width  = unit(width, "mm"),
                               height = unit(heigth_gc, "mm"))

# Save
ggsave(filename = file.path(dir_output, "Manuscript_figures", "A_growth_curves_Ccomes_chenodeoxycholic_acid.pdf"),
       plot = plot_egg,
       device = cairo_pdf(),
       width = width_block,
       height = heigth_block,
       unit = "mm",
       dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
  filter(SPECIES.name == "C.comes",
```

### Panel A - Chenodeoxycholic acid

```{r}
## _____________________________________________________
# AUC C. comes

# prepare data
plot_data = df_processed %>%
  filter(SPECIES.name == "C.comes",
         DRUG.name %in% c("DMSO", "BA-4"),
         REPLICATE %in% c(1, 3)) %>% 
  group_by(SPECIES.name, REPLICATE, DRUG.name, CONDITION) %>%
  summarise(AUC = mean(AUC, na.rm = TRUE),
            AUC.expo.end.gc = mean(AUC.expo.end.gc, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DRUG.name = factor(DRUG.name),
                SPECIES.name = factor(SPECIES.name),
                CONDITION = factor(CONDITION)) %>%
  rename(AUC.22h = AUC) %>%  
  pivot_longer(cols = c(AUC.22h, AUC.expo.end.gc),
               names_to = "METRIC.name",
               values_to = "METRIC.value") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(METRIC.name = factor(METRIC.name, levels = c("AUC.expo.end.gc", "AUC.22h"))) %>%
  mutate(DRUG.name = recode(DRUG.name,
                         "BA-4" = "Chenodeoxycholic acid",
                         "DMSO" = "DMSO"
                         )) %>% 
  mutate(DRUG.name = factor(DRUG.name, levels = c("DMSO","Chenodeoxycholic acid")))

# Save data:
data_A_comes = plot_data
# writexl::write_xlsx(data_A_comes, file.path(dir_output, "Manuscript_figures_data", "A_metrics_Ccomes_chenodeoxycholic_acid.xlsx"))

# plot
ggplot(data = plot_data,
       aes(x = DRUG.name, y = METRIC.value, fill = DRUG.name, shape = DRUG.name)) +
  facet_wrap(~METRIC.name, scales = "free") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.1))) +
  geom_point(size = 1, color = "black", position = position_jitter(width = 0.2)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("DMSO" = "white", "Chenodeoxycholic acid" = "#006290")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("DMSO" = 5, "Chenodeoxycholic acid" = 21)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  ggpubr::stat_pwc(
    method = "t.test",
    method.args = list(var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided"),
    p.adjust.method = "BH",
    label = "p.adj.format",
    hide.ns = F,
    label.size = 2,
    tip.length = 0,
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 6) +
  labs(
    title = "C. comes (n = 2)",
    y = "value",
    x = "",
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90", color = "black"),
  )

# egg
plot_egg = egg::set_panel_size(last_plot(),
                               width  = unit(width/2, "mm"),
                               height = unit(heigth, "mm"))

# Save
ggsave(filename = file.path(dir_output, "Manuscript_figures", "A_AUC_Ccomes_chenodeoxycholic_acid.pdf"),
       plot = plot_egg,
       device = cairo_pdf(),
       width = width_block,
       height = heigth_block,
       unit = "mm",
       dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("DMSO" = 5, "Taurochondeoxycholic acid" = 21)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  ggpubr::stat_pwc(
    method = "t.test",
    method.args = list(var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided"),
    p.adjust.method = "BH",
    label = "p.adj.format",
    hide.ns = F,
    label.size = 2,
    tip.length = 0,
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 6) +
  labs(
    title = "R. intestinalis (n = 3)",
    y = "value",
    x = "",
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90", color = "black"),
  )

# egg
plot_egg = egg::set_panel_size(last_plot(),
                               width  = unit(width/2, "mm"),
                               height = unit(heigth, "mm"))

# Save
ggsave(filename = file.path(dir_output, "Manuscript_figures", "B_AUC_Rint_Taurochondeoxycholic_acid.pdf"),
       plot = plot_egg,
       device = cairo_pdf(),
       width = width_block,
       height = heigth_block,
       unit = "mm",
       dpi = 300)
```

### Panel C - Taurolitocholic acid

```{r}
## _____________________________________________________
# AUC C. comes

# prepare data
plot_data = df_processed %>%
  filter(SPECIES.name == "C.comes",
         DRUG.name %in% c("DMSO", "BA-14"),
         REPLICATE %in% c(1, 3)) %>% 
  group_by(SPECIES.name, REPLICATE, DRUG.name, CONDITION) %>%
  summarise(AUC = mean(AUC, na.rm = TRUE),
            AUC.expo.end.gc = mean(AUC.expo.end.gc, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DRUG.name = factor(DRUG.name),
                SPECIES.name = factor(SPECIES.name),
                CONDITION = factor(CONDITION)) %>%
  rename(AUC.22h = AUC) %>%  
  pivot_longer(cols = c(AUC.22h, AUC.expo.end.gc),
               names_to = "METRIC.name",
               values_to = "METRIC.value") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(METRIC.name = factor(METRIC.name, levels = c("AUC.expo.end.gc", "AUC.22h"))) %>%
  mutate(DRUG.name = recode(DRUG.name,
                         "BA-14" = "Taurolitocholic acid",
                         "DMSO" = "DMSO"
                         )) %>% 
  mutate(DRUG.name = factor(DRUG.name, levels = c("DMSO","Taurolitocholic acid")))

# Save data:
```
